info.title: Asset Management API
info.summary: Deterministic portfolio analytics over a currency-aware ledger.

get.description:
Return every tracked portfolio, for the UI's portfolio picker.

Declared before ``/{portfolio_id}`` so FastAPI matches this literal path first.

schema.title: Response List Portfolios Api V1 Portfolios Get

post.description: Create a new empty portfolio and return its assigned identity.

get.description: Return a portfolio's identity + base currency (404 if it doesn't exist).
Return the portfolio's full ledger as typed transactions.

schema.title: Response List Transactions Api V1 Portfolios  Portfolio Id  Transactions Get

post.description: Append manually-entered ledger events (404 if the portfolio is absent).

get.description: Return the portfolio's tracked securities + classification metadata.

schema.title: Response List Holdings Api V1 Portfolios  Portfolio Id  Holdings Get

get.description: Return aggregated cost-basis / realized-P&L / XIRR analytics (404 if absent).

post.description:
Record current-holding snapshots as opening BUY lots (404 if absent).

This is the fast on-ramp for an existing portfolio: assert each position's
ticker, quantity, and cost basis instead of re-keying years of trades.

Backfill sector/industry for this portfolio's holdings from company profiles.

A broker statement carries no classification data, so imported holdings start
unclassified and the allocation breakdown groups them under ``UNCLASSIFIED``.
This fills them in from the market-data provider.

Already-classified holdings are skipped (so hand-entered labels survive) unless
``refresh=true``. At most ``limit`` tickers are processed per call to bound both
request time and free-tier quota use; repeat while ``remaining`` is non-zero.

Responds ``503`` when no market-data provider is configured — the remedy is an
API key, not a retry.

patch.description:
Manually set a holding's sector and/or industry (404 if it isn't held).

The manual path intentionally does not depend on market data: classification
must stay editable when the provider is unconfigured, rate-limited, or simply
wrong about a symbol.

post.description:
Accept a broker statement and process it in the background.

Returns ``202 Accepted`` immediately with a ``PENDING`` job — a decade-long
export can hold thousands of rows, far too slow to finish inside the request.
Poll ``GET /portfolios/{id}/imports/{job_id}`` until the status is terminal,
then refetch analytics.

The upload's declared ``content_type`` is untrusted browser metadata, so the
format comes from ``source_format`` and the parser validates the actual bytes.
Re-uploading identical content is rejected with ``409`` (it would double-count
the whole ledger); pass ``allow_duplicate=true`` to override deliberately.

get.description: Return the portfolio's import history, newest first.

schema.title: Response List Imports Api V1 Portfolios  Portfolio Id  Imports Get

get.description: Return one import job's live status/progress (the endpoint the UI polls).
Liveness probe — cheap check that the app is up (no DB touch).

CostBasisResult.description: Outcome of replaying a ticker's ledger under FIFO lot accounting.

HoldingClassificationResult.title: HoldingClassificationResult
HoldingClassificationResult.description:
Outcome of backfilling holdings' sector/industry from company profiles.

Split three ways so the caller can tell progress from failure:

* ``classified`` — holdings that now carry a sector and/or industry.
* ``unresolved`` — the provider returned nothing usable (unknown symbol,
  quota exhausted, upstream down). Retrying later may succeed.
* ``skipped``    — already classified, so no upstream call was spent on them.

``remaining`` reports how many unclassified holdings were left untouched
because the per-request ``limit`` was reached, so a caller knows to call again
rather than assuming the backfill is complete.

HoldingClassificationUpdate.title: HoldingClassificationUpdate
HoldingClassificationUpdate.description:
Manual sector/industry override for one holding.

Both fields are optional so a caller can correct just one of them, but at
least one must be present — an empty body is a no-op request, not an
instruction to erase the classification. Clearing a value is deliberately not
expressible here: allocation grouping already represents "unknown" as the
``UNCLASSIFIED`` bucket, so blanking a field has no separate meaning.

MoneyWeightedReturnStatus.title: MoneyWeightedReturnStatus
MoneyWeightedReturnStatus.description:
Why the money-weighted return (XIRR) is, or is not, a number.

A bare ``null`` cannot distinguish "this portfolio has too little history to
have a return" from "we could not price your open positions today". Those
call for completely different user action — enter more history versus
configure market data — so the reason travels with the value.

OpenLot.title: OpenLot
OpenLot.description: An unclosed FIFO purchase lot, valued in the portfolio base currency.

PortfolioAnalytics.title: PortfolioAnalytics
PortfolioAnalytics.description:
Aggregated, base-currency portfolio analytics (the service layer's output).

This is the single typed envelope the ``/analytics`` endpoint returns. It bundles
the portfolio identity, per-position FIFO cost-basis results, whole-portfolio
roll-up totals, and the money-weighted return (XIRR).

``money_weighted_return`` is ``None`` whenever XIRR is not trustworthy, and
``money_weighted_return_status`` says why — we surface "not computable"
honestly rather than emitting a misleading ``0``. It is a *rate* (annualized
fraction), not money, but is kept as ``Decimal`` so no ``float`` leaks into a
financial payload.

Note that XIRR on a portfolio holding open positions requires a **terminal
value**: today's market value, treated as the inflow you would receive on
liquidating. Without it a buy-only ledger has only negative flows and no root
exists. That is why the return depends on market data being available, and why
it is withheld (``UNPRICED_POSITIONS``) when any open position lacks a price.

Market-value-dependent figures — per-position unrealized P&L and allocation
weights — are populated when the market-data provider supplies current
prices. When prices are unavailable (no provider configured, quota exhausted,
or a missing FX rate) those fields degrade gracefully: totals are ``None``,
allocation lists are empty, and the affected tickers are reported in
``unpriced_tickers`` so the omission is explicit, never a silent ``0``.

PositionSnapshot.title: PositionSnapshot
PositionSnapshot.description:
A user's *current* holding, captured without full transaction history.

This is the answer to "my portfolio is 10 years old and I don't want to key in
every trade": you assert the position as it stands today — how many shares you
hold and what they cost — and the system records it as a single opening ``BUY``
lot in the ledger. Every downstream calculator then treats it like any other
lot, so cost-basis and unrealized P&L are exact.

Provide the cost basis exactly one of two ways (brokerages report both):

* ``cost_basis_per_share`` — the average price paid per share, or
* ``total_cost_basis`` — the aggregate amount invested (we divide by quantity).

``as_of`` is the acquisition/opening date. When you genuinely don't know it,
leave it unset and the service stamps today's date — but note the money-weighted
return (XIRR) is only meaningful with a *real* purchase date, so a snapshot with
a placeholder date will (correctly) leave XIRR undefined while cost-basis and
unrealized P&L stay exact.

StatementFormat.title: StatementFormat
StatementFormat.description: Supported broker statement layouts for the import endpoint.

StatementImportStatus.title: StatementImportStatus
StatementImportStatus.description:
Progress + outcome of one statement import (what the UI polls).

A decade-long export can hold thousands of rows, so the upload endpoint returns
immediately with this record in ``PENDING`` and the work continues in the
background. The client polls until ``status`` is terminal.

``processed_rows``/``total_rows`` drive a progress bar. ``total_rows`` is
``None`` until parsing has counted the file, because an honest "unknown" is
better than a fake denominator that makes a progress bar jump backwards.

Transaction-Input.title: Transaction
Transaction-Input.description:
A single dated ledger event for one ticker, in its native currency.

Field usage by ``type``:

* ``BUY`` / ``SELL``: ``quantity`` (> 0) and ``price`` per share; ``fees`` optional.
* ``DIVIDEND``: ``amount`` = total cash received (native currency).
* ``FEE``: ``amount`` = total fee paid (native currency).
* ``SPLIT``: ``split_ratio`` (e.g. ``2`` for a 2-for-1); other fields ignored.
